iPhone wave profiling

Fixed test scene: sunny, 3 ft / 8 s, zero tide, 8 kt wind, resting beach camera, DPR 2. Test values, not a live forecast.

Open in iPhone Safari. Keep this page foregrounded and avoid screen recording while measuring. The full suite takes several minutes plus loading. It repeats the baseline at the end to expose warming or thermal drift.

Round 5: baseline → clear only with GPU wait → clear only without wait → native with CPU readbacks and wait removed → native with only wait removed → baseline. DPR 2 throughout. Logs parent rAF cadence, synchronous JS time, skipped frames and final queue drain.

Round 4: one native renderer, full High waves. DPR 2 → 1.75 → 1.5 → FXAA at DPR 2 → flare off at DPR 2 → DPR 2 again. Other settings stay fixed in each row.

Round 3: ocean ON, High detail and DPR 2 throughout. Baseline → proof alone → second layer removed → shadows off → background baked / atmosphere frozen → post/composition bypass → all four cuts → baseline. These cuts deliberately change the picture; they are diagnostics only.

Round 2 brackets the one-transfer candidate with unchanged baselines, then tests DPR 1.0, DPR 1.5, all-ocean-off, 3 × 128 FFT and one-step lower mesh LOD separately. The ordinary app is unchanged. Lower-DPR rows are diagnostic only.

Reported round 4: ~19.98 fps across native variants. Round 5 tests the completion gate and CPU readbacks. “rAF submit” counts submissions, not finished GPU work or displayed frames. A large final drain means queued work; higher rAF FPS alone cannot establish the 30 fps target.
